q: Identify the error: 'Neither the manager nor his assistants was willing to take responsibility.'
exp: With 'neither...nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject. Since 'assistants' is plural, 'were willing' is required.

q: Identify the error: 'Each of the employees have submitted their report.'
exp: 'Each' is singular and requires 'has submitted', not 'have submitted'.

q: Choose the best replacement for the underlined phrase: 'He is senior than me in the organization.'
exp: The standard construction is 'senior to', so 'senior to me' is correct.

q: Identify the error: 'The news are very encouraging for the investors.'
exp: 'News' is treated as a singular uncountable noun, so the correct phrase is 'The news is very encouraging'.

q: Identify the error: 'She is one of the best employee in the branch.'
exp: After 'one of the best', the noun should be plural: 'employees'.

q: Identify the error: 'Hardly had I reached the station when the train had left.'
exp: With 'hardly had', the later event is normally expressed in simple past: 'when the train left'.

q: Choose the best replacement: 'The report comprises of five sections.'
exp: The verb 'comprise' is normally used directly with the object: 'comprises five sections'.

q: Identify the error: 'He discussed about the new project with his team.'
exp: 'Discuss' is a transitive verb and does not require 'about'. The correct form is 'He discussed the new project'.

q: Choose the best replacement: 'Despite of the heavy rain, the match continued.'
exp: 'Despite' is used directly before a noun phrase and does not take 'of'.

q: Choose the best replacement: 'The manager as well as his assistants are attending the meeting.'
exp: With 'as well as', the verb agrees with the main subject 'manager', which is singular. Therefore 'is attending' is correct.

q: Fill in the blank: The manager asked the employees to submit the documents ___ Friday.
exp: 'By Friday' means on or before Friday and correctly expresses the deadline.

q: Fill in the blank: If the company ___ the proposal carefully, it would have avoided the mistake.
exp: This is a third conditional structure: 'If ... had examined, it would have avoided'.

q: Fill in the blank: The committee has decided to ___ the issue before making a final recommendation.
exp: 'Look into' means to investigate or examine something carefully.

q: Fill in the blank: The new policy is expected to bring ___ major changes in the recruitment process.
exp: 'Several' correctly modifies the plural countable noun 'changes'.

q: Fill in the blank: Unless you ___ the instructions carefully, you may make a mistake.
exp: In a first conditional sentence with 'unless', the present simple is used in the condition clause: 'Unless you read...'.
